heroHeadline: Sudan Accuses UAE and Ethiopia of Orchestrating Khartoum Airport Drone Attacks; Ambassador Recalled on Day 1117
heroSubtitle: On May 5, 2026 (Day 1116), an RSF/UAE drone was intercepted by SAF air defenses over Khartoum International Airport — the same airport that had welcomed its first commercial flight since the war began just days earlier. Sudan's military presented evidence of four drone attacks since March 1 originating from Ethiopia's Bahir Dar airport, identifying a serial number traceable to UAE manufacture (S88). Foreign Minister Mohieddin Salem recalled Sudan's ambassador to Ethiopia and announced Sudan would submit the evidence to the UN Security Council, warning of 'open confrontation with Ethiopia if it becomes necessary.' Both Ethiopia and the UAE denied involvement. On May 6, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, the US, and EU condemned the attacks but stopped short of endorsing Sudan's accusations. The airport suspended all operations for 72 hours. The escalation comes as drone warfare continues to ravage civilian areas across Sudan: SAF struck Balila market in Kurmuk, Blue Nile State on May 4, killing 7–10 civilians; RSF drones killed 5 in a vehicle near Omdurman on May 2 and 9–17 members of defector commander Kaikal's family in Gezira; and on April 30, an RSF drone killed 27 SAF commanders in Singa during a high-level meeting. Approximately 700 civilians died in drone strikes in Q1 2026, and 34 million people — 65% of Sudan's population — remain in urgent need of humanitarian support.
